\textbf{ENEL445 Full Exam Cheat Sheet — Q1 Roy Smith + Q2 Power Systems / Game Theory / LMI}

\section*{Core Math Templates}

\subsection*{Matrix Derivatives / Taylor}

For scalar $f(\mathbf x)$:
$$
f(\mathbf x)\approx f(\mathbf c)+\nabla f(\mathbf c)^T(\mathbf x-\mathbf c)+\frac12(\mathbf x-\mathbf c)^TH(\mathbf c)(\mathbf x-\mathbf c).
$$

\Pp{Quadratic}:
$$
f(\mathbf x)=\mathbf x^TA\mathbf x,\quad \nabla f=(A+A^T)\mathbf x,\quad A=A^T\Rightarrow \nabla f=2A\mathbf x.
$$

$$
f(\mathbf x)=\frac12\mathbf x^TA\mathbf x+\mathbf b^T\mathbf x+c,\quad A=A^T
\Rightarrow \nabla f=A\mathbf x+\mathbf b,\ H=A.
$$

\Pp{PSD/PD}:
$$
A\succeq0\Leftrightarrow \mathbf z^TA\mathbf z\ge0\ \forall \mathbf z;\quad
A\succ0\Leftrightarrow \mathbf z^TA\mathbf z>0\ \forall \mathbf z\ne0.
$$
Stationary + $H\succ0$ $\Rightarrow$ strict local min. Convex twice differentiable: $H(x)\succeq0$.

\Pp{Newton}:
$$
\mathbf x_{k+1}=\mathbf x_k-H(\mathbf x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(\mathbf x_k),\quad
\mathbf p_k=-H(\mathbf x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(\mathbf x_k).
$$
If $H(\mathbf x_k)\succ0$: $\nabla f(\mathbf x_k)^T\mathbf p_k<0$ unless $\nabla f(\mathbf x_k)=0$.

Exact line search for quadratic $f=\frac12x^TAx+b^Tx$ along $p$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\phi(\mu)&=f(c+\mu p),\\
\phi'(\mu)&=p^T(Ac+b)+\mu p^TAp=0,\\
\mu^*&=-\frac{p^T(Ac+b)}{p^TAp}.
\end{aligned}
$$

\subsection*{Lagrangian / KKT}

For $\min f(x)$ s.t. $g_i(x)\le0,\ h_j(x)=0$:
$$
L=f+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i+\sum_j\nu_jh_j,\quad \lambda_i\ge0.
$$
\Pp{KKT}: stationarity $\nabla_xL=0$; primal feasible $g_i(x)\le0,h_j(x)=0$; dual feasible $\lambda_i\ge0$; complementarity $\lambda_i g_i(x)=0$.  
\W{Bounds sign}: $u\le u_{\max}\Rightarrow u-u_{\max}\le0$; $u\ge u_{\min}\Rightarrow u_{\min}-u\le0$.

Convex + regularity $\Rightarrow$ KKT iff global optimum. Nonconvex: KKT usually only local necessary/candidate.

\section*{Q1 Roy: Least Squares}

\subsection*{LS Formulation}

\Pp{Model}:
$$
y=\Phi\theta+\epsilon,\quad r=y-\Phi\theta,\quad
\min_\theta\|y-\Phi\theta\|_2^2.
$$
\Pp{Normal equations}:
$$
\begin{aligned}
J&=(y-\Phi\theta)^T(y-\Phi\theta)\\
&=y^Ty-2\theta^T\Phi^Ty+\theta^T\Phi^T\Phi\theta,\\
\nabla_\theta J&=-2\Phi^Ty+2\Phi^T\Phi\theta=0
\Rightarrow \Phi^T\Phi\hat\theta=\Phi^Ty,\quad
\hat\theta=(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^Ty
\end{aligned}
$$
if full column rank. Residual orthogonality:
$$
\Phi^T(y-\Phi\hat\theta)=0.
$$
\Pp{Projection}: $\hat y=\Phi\hat\theta=P_\Phi y$, $r\perp \operatorname{col}(\Phi)$.

\Pp{Watch dimensions}: $\Phi:N\times d$, $\theta:d\times1$, $\Phi^T\Phi:d\times d$.

\subsection*{Unbiasedness / Covariance / CI}

Assume fixed $\Phi$, full rank, $E[\epsilon]=0$:
$$
\hat\theta=(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^T(\Phi\theta_0+\epsilon)
=\theta_0+(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^T\epsilon
\Rightarrow E[\hat\theta]=\theta_0.
$$
If $\operatorname{Cov}(\epsilon)=\sigma^2I$:
$$
\hat\theta-\theta_0=A\epsilon,\quad A=(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^T,
\quad \operatorname{Cov}(A\epsilon)=A\operatorname{Cov}(\epsilon)A^T
=\sigma^2(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}.
$$
Ill-conditioned $\Phi^T\Phi$ $\Rightarrow$ large variance/unstable coefficients.  
\Pp{Coefficient SE}: $\operatorname{se}(\hat\theta_j)=\hat\sigma\sqrt{[(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}]_{jj}}$.  
\Pp{CI}: $\hat\theta_j\pm t_{\alpha/2,N-d}\operatorname{se}(\hat\theta_j)$.

CI smaller $\Leftrightarrow$ estimator more stable / lower variance.

\subsection*{BLUE / Weighted LS}

General noise covariance $R=\operatorname{Cov}(\epsilon)=E[\epsilon\epsilon^T]$:
$$
\hat\theta_{\rm BLUE}=(\Phi^TR^{-1}\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^TR^{-1}y,
\quad \operatorname{Cov}(\hat\theta_{\rm BLUE})=(\Phi^TR^{-1}\Phi)^{-1}.
$$
BLUE minimises **variance among unbiased linear estimators**, not MSE over biased estimators.

\Pp{Inverse-variance weights for independent unbiased estimates}:
$$
\hat\theta_w=\sum_iw_i\hat\theta_i,\quad \sum_iw_i=1,\quad
\min_w\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta_w)=\min_w\sum_iw_i^2\sigma_i^2
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L&=\sum_iw_i^2\sigma_i^2+\lambda(\sum_iw_i-1)\\
2w_i\sigma_i^2+\lambda&=0\Rightarrow w_i\propto1/\sigma_i^2,\quad
w_i=\frac{1/\sigma_i^2}{\sum_j1/\sigma_j^2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

\subsection*{Bias / Variance / MSE / Metric}

$$
\operatorname{Bias}(\hat\theta)=E[\hat\theta]-\theta,\quad
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta)=E[(\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta])^2],
$$
$$
\operatorname{MSE}(\hat\theta)=E[(\hat\theta-\theta)^2].
$$
\Pp{Derivation}:
$$
\hat\theta-\theta
=\big(\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta]\big)+\big(E[\hat\theta]-\theta\big).
$$
$$
\operatorname{MSE}
=E[(\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta])^2]
+2(E[\hat\theta]-\theta)E[\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta]]
+(E[\hat\theta]-\theta)^2
$$
since $E[\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta]]=E[\hat\theta]-E[\hat\theta]=0$.
$$
=\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta)+\operatorname{Bias}(\hat\theta)^2.
$$
\Pp{Prediction/safety/control}: prefer lower variance/stable estimates. Scientific parameter interpretation: bias of a particular coefficient may matter more than total MSE. Metric follows purpose.

\subsection*{Regularisation}

\Pp{Ridge}:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_\theta \frac12\|y-\Phi\theta\|_2^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\theta\|_2^2
&\Rightarrow \nabla J=-\Phi^Ty+\Phi^T\Phi\theta+\lambda\theta=0,\\
&\Rightarrow(\Phi^T\Phi+\lambda I)\hat\theta=\Phi^Ty.
\end{aligned}
$$
\Pp{Stability}: $\lambda I$ lifts small singular/eigenvalues, improves conditioning, lowers variance, adds bias.

\Pp{Tikhonov}:
$$
\min_\theta\|y-\Phi\theta\|^2+\|R\theta\|^2
\Rightarrow(\Phi^T\Phi+R^TR)\theta=\Phi^Ty.
$$
$R$ useful if structured; arbitrary $R$ creates too many hyperparameters.R should encode prior structure / known smoothness / meaningful parameter penalties.

\Pp{LASSO}: $\|y-\Phi\theta\|^2+\lambda\|\theta\|_1$; sparse, variable selection, no closed form generally.  
\Pp{Elastic Net}: $\lambda_1\|\theta\|_1+\lambda_2\|\theta\|_2^2$; sparse + handles correlated predictors.

\Pp{Rule}: Ridge many weak signals; LASSO few useful signals; Elastic Net correlated/varying signals. Use validation/CV for $\lambda$.

\Pp{Engineering order}: better $\Phi$ first (variables, measurements, experiment design), regularisation second.

\section*{Q1 Roy: Convex Geometry}

\Pp{Convex set}:
$$
x,y\in C,\ \alpha\in[0,1]\Rightarrow \alpha x+(1-\alpha)y\in C.
$$
\Pp{Cone}:
$$
x\in C,\ \gamma\ge0\Rightarrow\gamma x\in C.
$$
\Pp{Convex cone}:
$$
x_i\in C,\ \gamma_i\ge0\Rightarrow \sum_i\gamma_ix_i\in C.
$$

\Pp{Hyperplane}: $\{x\mid a^Tx=b\}$; halfspace $\{x\mid a^Tx\le b\}$. $a$ is normal. One equality removes one degree of freedom.  
\Pp{Polyhedron}: $\{x\mid Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}$. Test feasible side by substituting a point.

\Pp{Norm ball}: $\{x\mid\|x-x_c\|\le r\}$. Norm cone/SOC:
$$
\mathcal Q^{n+1}=\{(t,x)\mid \|x\|_2\le t\}.
$$
\Pp{Ellipsoid}:
$$
\{x\mid(x-x_c)^TP^{-1}(x-x_c)\le1\},\ P\succ0.
$$

\Pp{Convex function}:
$$
x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ \alpha\in[0,1]\Rightarrow
f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\le\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),
$$
$\operatorname{dom}f$ must be convex. Strict convex: unique minimiser if exists. Norms are convex.

\Pp{Quasi-convex}:
$$
S_\alpha=\{x\mid f(x)\le\alpha\}\ \text{sublevel set, convex for all }\alpha.
$$
Bisection searches value $\alpha$ by bracketing: feasible $\Rightarrow$ lower upper bound; infeasible $\Rightarrow$ raise lower bound. Keep squeezing $[L,U]$ until tight.

\Pp{Line search}: Armijo/backtracking searches step size $t$ along descent direction $d$:
$$
x^+=x+td,\quad
f(x+td)\le f(x)+ct\nabla f(x)^Td,\quad 0<c<1.
$$
Start $t=1$; if fail, $t\leftarrow\beta t$ ($0<\beta<1$). Bisection = global/value/feasibility; Armijo = local/step/gradient.

\Pp{Ellipsoid method}: keep ellipsoid containing optimum; gradient/subgradient/violated constraint gives halfspace cut; wrap kept half with smaller ellipsoid. Theory/LP polynomial-time proof; not practical first-choice solver.

\section*{Q1/Q2: Cone, SDP, LMI, Schur}

\Pp{Cone language}:
$$
Ax\le b\Leftrightarrow b-Ax\in\mathbb R_+^m.
$$
$\mathbb R_+^m=\{z\in\mathbb R^m\mid z_i\ge0\ \forall i\}$.

\Pp{PSD cone}:
$$
S_+^n=\{X=X^T\mid X\succeq0\}.
$$
\Pp{LMI}: affine symmetric matrix constrained to PSD cone:
$$
F(x)=F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i\succeq0\quad(\Leftrightarrow F(x)\in S_+^n).
$$
\Pp{For $2\times2$}:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{bmatrix}\succeq0
\Leftrightarrow a\ge0,\ c\ge0,\ ac-b^2\ge0.
$$
\Pp{Example}: $\begin{bmatrix}2&x\\x&8\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\Rightarrow16-x^2\ge0\Rightarrow |x|\le4$.

\Pp{Schur complement theorem}:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}Q&S\\S^T&R\end{bmatrix}\succ0,\ R\succ0
\Leftrightarrow Q-SR^{-1}S^T\succ0.
$$
\Pp{Use}: with $R\succ0$, test big block matrix PD by testing the smaller Schur matrix $Q-SR^{-1}S^T$.
\Pp{Why}: test quadratic form, then complete square in $v$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
[u^T,v^T]\begin{bmatrix}Q&S\\S^T&R\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}
&=u^TQu+2u^TSv+v^TRv\\
u^TQu+2u^TSv+v^TRv
&=(v+R^{-1}S^Tu)^TR(v+R^{-1}S^Tu)\\
&\quad+u^T(Q-SR^{-1}S^T)u.
\end{aligned}
$$
Since $R\succ0$, first square term $\ge0$; PD depends on the leftover Schur term.
\Pp{Also with signs}:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}Q&S\\S^T&R\end{bmatrix}\preceq0,\ R\prec0
\Leftrightarrow Q-SR^{-1}S^T\preceq0.
$$

\Pp{Purpose}: convert suitable quadratic/inverse constraints into affine PSD constraints, so convex SDP/LMI solvers can handle them.

\Pp{Quadratic constraint to LMI}, need $Q\succ0$ not just $Q\succeq0$:
$$
x^TQx+b^Tx+c\le0
\Leftrightarrow
\begin{bmatrix}
c+b^Tx & x^T\\
x & -Q^{-1}
\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.
$$
\Pp{Check}: Schur on $-Q^{-1}\prec0$ gives $c+b^Tx+x^TQx\le0$.

\Pp{SOC/norm to LMI}:
$$
\|Ax+b\|_2\le c^Tx+d,\ t=c^Tx+d
$$
\W{Hidden condition}: requires $t\ge0$ and
$$
\begin{bmatrix}
tI & Ax+b\\
(Ax+b)^T & t
\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.
$$
\Pp{Schur}: $t-(Ax+b)^T(tI)^{-1}(Ax+b)\ge0\Rightarrow t^2\ge\|Ax+b\|^2$.

\Pp{Spectral norm}:
$$
\|A(x)\|_2<\gamma
\Leftrightarrow
\begin{bmatrix}\gamma I&A(x)\\A(x)^T&\gamma I\end{bmatrix}\succ0.
$$
\W{Hidden condition} $\gamma>0$. Schur: $\gamma I-\gamma^{-1}AA^T\succ0\Leftrightarrow \gamma^2I-AA^T\succ0$. \T{Why LMI?} every entry affine in $(x,\gamma)$.

\Pp{Epigraph trick}:
$$
\min f(x)\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad \min t\ \text{s.t. } f(x)\le t.
$$
This turns nonlinear objective into constraint plus linear cost.

\subsection*{Lyapunov / Control LMI}

\Pp{Discrete stability}: $x_{k+1}=Ax_k$ stable if $\exists P\succ0$ with $A^TPA-P\prec0$. Schur form:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}-P&A^T\\A&-P^{-1}\end{bmatrix}\prec0.
$$
Schur on $-P^{-1}$ gives $-P+A^TPA\prec0$. Congruence transform preserves definiteness: $M\prec0$, nonsingular $T$ $\Rightarrow T^TMT\prec0$. State feedback $u=Kx$, closed loop $A+BK$; substitute $Y=P^{-1}$, $L=KY$ to make LMIs linear.
Example scalar $x_{k+1}=ax_k$: choose $P=1$, $a^2P-P<0\Rightarrow a^2-1<0\Rightarrow |a|<1$.

\section*{Q1 Roy: MPC}

\Pp{Dynamics}: $x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k+Fw_k$. Finite horizon:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\{x_i,u_i\}} \quad
& \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}(x_i-r_i)^TQ(x_i-r_i)\\
&+\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}u_i^TRu_i+(x_N-r_N)^TQ_f(x_N-r_N)\\
\text{s.t.}\quad &x_{i+1}=Ax_i+Bu_i,\quad x_0=x_k,\\
&u_{\min}\le u_i\le u_{\max},\quad x_i\in\mathcal X,\quad x_N\in\mathcal X_f.
\end{aligned}
$$

\Pp{Meaning}: $x_k$ state vector; $u_k$ control input; $N$ prediction horizon; $r_i$ reference/target trajectory. $A$ natural dynamics; $B$ input effect; $Q$ tracking/state weight; $R$ control-effort weight. High $Q$/low $R$ = aggressive; high $R$ = smooth/conservative.

\Pp{MPC loop}: measure/estimate $x_k$ -> optimise future trajectory -> apply first $u_k$ -> repeat. Linear dynamics + quadratic cost + linear bounds $\Rightarrow$ QP after stacking:
$z=[x_0^T,\dots,x_N^T,u_0^T,\dots,u_{N-1}^T]^T$, $J=\frac12z^THz+f^Tz+\text{const}$, $Gz\le h,\ Ez=e$. $H$ from $Q,R,Q_f$; $f$ from reference. Nonlinear dynamics/cost/constraints or integer vars break standard QP.

\Pp{Explicit MPC one-step}:
$$
J=x_{k+1}^TQx_{k+1}+u_k^TRu_k,\quad x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k.
$$
\Pp{Substitute}: $J=x_k^TA^TQAx_k+2x_k^TA^TQBu_k+u_k^T(B^TQB+R)u_k$.  
Let scalar input $H=B^TQB+R>0$, $g=B^TQA$. Interior:
$2gx_k+2Hu_k=0\Rightarrow u_k^*=-H^{-1}gx_k$.  
With bounds $u-u_{\max}\le0$, $u_{\min}-u\le0$:
$L=J+\lambda_u(u-u_{\max})+\lambda_l(u_{\min}-u)$,
$2gx_k+2Hu+\lambda_u-\lambda_l=0$.
\Pp{Bounds}:
$u^*(x)=\min\{u_{\max},\max\{u_{\min},-H^{-1}gx\}\}$.
\Pp{Regions}: $u^*=u_{\max}$ if $gx_k\le-Hu_{\max}$; $u^*=-H^{-1}gx_k$ if $-Hu_{\max}\le gx_k\le-Hu_{\min}$; $u^*=u_{\min}$ if $gx_k\ge-Hu_{\min}$.

\section*{Q2 Power Systems}

\subsection*{Economic Dispatch / Pricing}

\Pp{ED}:
$$
\min_{P_{G_i}}\sum_i C_i(P_{G_i}),\quad
\sum_iP_{G_i}=P_D,\quad P_i^{\min}\le P_{G_i}\le P_i^{\max}.
$$
\Pp{No active limits/no losses}:
$$
\begin{aligned}
L&=\sum_iC_i(P_i)+\lambda(P_D-\sum_iP_i),\\
\partial L/\partial P_i&=C_i'(P_i)-\lambda=0
\Rightarrow C_i'(P_i)=\lambda.
\end{aligned}
$$
\Pp{With losses}:
$$
P_D+P_L(P_G)-\sum_iP_{G_i}=0,\quad
L_i=\frac1{1-\partial P_L/\partial P_{G_i}},
$$
\Pp{optimal}:
$$
L_iIC_i(P_{G_i})=\lambda.
$$

\Pp{Uniform price}: all accepted generators paid marginal clearing price. Pay-as-bid: each paid own bid; more strategic bidding.

\Pp{ED KKT with bounds}: $L=C+\lambda(P_D-\sum_iP_i)+\sum_i\mu_i^-(P_i^{\min}-P_i)+\sum_i\mu_i^+(P_i-P_i^{\max})$.  
\Pp{Stationarity}: $C_i'(P_i)-\lambda-\mu_i^-+\mu_i^+=0$; complementarity: $\mu_i^-(P_i^{\min}-P_i)=0$, $\mu_i^+(P_i-P_i^{\max})=0$.

\Pp{LMP intuition}: no congestion/loss $\Rightarrow$ same marginal price everywhere. Congestion/losses make bus prices differ; shadow prices on line limits enter local marginal cost.

\subsection*{OPF Types}

\Pp{OPF} = Optimal Power Flow: choose generation/control variables to minimise cost subject to power-flow equations and operating limits.  
\Pp{ED}: generation cost + total balance, ignores network.  
\Pp{DC OPF}: linear active-power flows and line limits; fast real-time approximation.  
\Pp{AC OPF}: full $P,Q,V,\theta$ nonlinear AC equations; accurate but large/nonconvex.  
\Pp{SC-OPF}: base case + \W{contingencies} (outage/disturbance cases: line/gen/transformer outage), much larger.

\Pp{AC OPF hard}: many vars/constraints; $\sin,\cos$; nonlinear/nonconvex equalities; real-time; SC constraints multiply cases.  
\Pp{Mitigate}: DC OPF, linearisation, piecewise loss approximation, warm start, interior-point, decomposition, contingency screening, AC feasibility check after DC OPF.

\Pp{Interior-point barrier}:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\min f(x)\ \text{s.t. }g_i(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\\
\Rightarrow\ 
\min \left[f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log(-g_i(x))\right]
\ \text{s.t. }h(x)=0.
\end{gathered}
$$

\Pp{Scaling}:
$$
t_2/t_1\approx(N_2/N_1)^3,\quad
t_{AC}\approx5t_{DC}(N_{AC}/N_{DC})^3.
$$
\Pp{Example}: $N_{AC}=2N_{DC}\Rightarrow t_{AC}\approx40t_{DC}$.

\subsection*{DC Power Flow / DC OPF}

\Pp{Assumptions}: $V_i\approx1$ p.u.; ignore $Q$; small angles; lossless/negligible resistance.
$$
\sin(\theta_i-\theta_j)\approx\theta_i-\theta_j,\quad
P_{ij}=B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j).
$$
DC OPF is DC **approximation** of AC grid, not DC electrical grid.

\subsection*{State Estimation}

\Pp{General}:
$$
z=h(x)+e,\quad
\min_x(z-h(x))^TR^{-1}(z-h(x)).
$$
\Pp{Equal variances}: $\min_x\|z-h(x)\|_2^2$. Linear $h(x)=Hx$:
$$
\hat x=(H^TH)^{-1}H^Tz,\quad
\hat x_W=(H^TR^{-1}H)^{-1}H^TR^{-1}z.
$$
Need reference angle because only angle differences observable.

\Pp{DC SE template}: measurements
$$
z=[P_{12}^m,P_{13}^m,P_{32}^m]^T,\quad P_{ij}=B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j).
$$
Set $\theta_1=0$, $x=[\theta_2,\theta_3]^T$:
$$
H=\begin{bmatrix}
-B_{12}&0\\
0&-B_{13}\\
-B_{32}&B_{32}
\end{bmatrix},\quad
\min_x\|z-Hx\|_2^2.
$$

\Pp{AC NLS}:
$$
P_{ij}=V_iV_jB_{ij}\sin(\theta_i-\theta_j),
$$
$$
Q_{ij}=V_i(V_i-V_j\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j))B_{ij}.
$$
Choose state, e.g. $x=[V_1,V_2,V_3,\theta_2,\theta_3]^T$ with $\theta_1=0$; stack measurements into $z$ and predictions into $h(x)$:
$$
\min_x\|z-h(x)\|_2^2
$$
Use the weighted version if variances differ. If a parameter is unknown, e.g. $B_{32}$, include it in $x$.
\Pp{Example}: $z=[P_{12}^m,Q_{12}^m,P_{13}^m,Q_{13}^m,V_1^m]^T$ and $h(x)=[P_{12}(x),Q_{12}(x),P_{13}(x),Q_{13}(x),V_1]^T$.

\Pp{Per unit}: $P_{\rm pu}=P_{\rm actual}/S_{\rm base}$.

\section*{Q2 Game Theory}

\Pp{Game theory}: each player chooses a strategy to maximise their own payoff; the outcome is an equilibrium, not necessarily the global/social optimum.

\Pp{Payoff matrix}: reward matrix $\Rightarrow$ larger is better; cost/sentence matrix $\Rightarrow$ smaller is better. For each column find row player's BR; for each row find column player's BR; double-marked cell = \K{Nash equilibrium}. \W{NE is strategy profile}; payoff is separate.

\Pp{Nash equilibrium}:
$$
s^*=(s_1^*,...,s_n^*)\quad
u_i(s_i^*,s_{-i}^*)\ge u_i(s_i,s_{-i}^*)\ \forall s_i,\forall i.
$$
No player can improve payoff by unilateral deviation while others keep their strategies fixed. NE $\ne$ social optimum.

\Pp{Dominant strategy}: best response regardless of opponent action. Dominated strategy: worse than another strategy for every opponent action.

Prisoner's dilemma: both players have dominant defect; NE $(D,D)$; social optimum $(C,C)$; individual rationality can be collectively inefficient.

\Pp{Maximax}: choose best possible payoff (optimistic).  
\Pp{Maximin}: choose best worst-case payoff (conservative).  
\Pp{Minimax}: minimise maximum loss/regret (robust).

\Pp{Zero-sum}: $u_1=-u_2$. Simultaneous game: Cournot. Sequential game: Stackelberg. Dynamic game: multiple stages/time.

\Pp{Cournot worked example}: two firms choose quantities $x_1,x_2$ simultaneously:
$$
U_1=12x_1-x_1^2-x_1x_2,\quad
\frac{\partial U_1}{\partial x_1}=12-2x_1-x_2=0
$$
$$
BR_1(x_2)=6-\frac{x_2}{2},\quad
BR_2(x_1)=6-\frac{x_1}{2}.
$$
\Pp{Solve BRs}: $x_1=6-x_2/2$, $x_2=6-x_1/2$
$\Rightarrow 2x_1+x_2=12$, $x_1+2x_2=12\Rightarrow x_1=x_2=4$.

\Pp{Stackelberg worked example}: leader chooses $x_1$ first; follower observes and chooses $x_2=BR_2(x_1)=6-x_1/2$. Substitute into leader payoff:
$$
U_1(x_1,BR_2)=12x_1-x_1^2-x_1(6-x_1/2)=6x_1-\frac12x_1^2
$$
\Pp{FOC}: $6-x_1=0\Rightarrow x_1^*=6,\ x_2^*=3$.

\Pp{General Cournot/Stackelberg}: if $P(Q)=a-bQ$, $\pi_i=(P-c)q_i$:
Cournot $q_1^*=q_2^*=(a-c)/(3b)$; Stackelberg leader $q_1^*=(a-c)/(2b)$, follower $q_2^*=(a-c)/(4b)$.

\Pp{Mixed strategy $2\times2$}: make opponent indifferent. If row payoff is $\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}$ and column plays first column with prob. $q$, solve
$qa+(1-q)b=qc+(1-q)d
\Rightarrow q=\frac{d-b}{a-b-c+d}$. Do the analogous equation for the column player.

\section*{Fast Classification / Common Traps}

\Pp{LP}: linear objective, linear constraints.  
\Pp{QP}: quadratic objective, linear constraints. OLS is QP; constrained LS no normal-equation closed form.  
\Pp{QCQP}: quadratic objective + quadratic constraints.  
\Pp{SOCP}: norm cone constraints $\|Ax+b\|\le c^Tx+d$.  
\Pp{SDP/LMI}: affine matrix constrained PSD.

\Pp{Convex optimisation standard}:
$$
\min f_0(x),\quad f_i(x)\le0,\quad Ax=b
$$
with convex $f_i$, affine equality. Nonlinear equality generally nonconvex.

\Pp{LP standard form}: max $\to$ min by negating; free $x=x^+-x^-$, $x^\pm\ge0$; $\le$ add slack; $\ge$ subtract surplus.

\section*{Roy Copy Templates}

\Pp{OLS unbiased}:
$y=\Phi\theta_0+\epsilon$, $E[\epsilon]=0$,
$$
\hat\theta=(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^Ty
=\theta_0+(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^T\epsilon
\Rightarrow E[\hat\theta]=\theta_0.
$$

\Pp{Ridge derivation}:
$$
J=\frac12\|y-\Phi\theta\|^2+\frac\lambda2\theta^T\theta,\quad
\nabla J=-\Phi^Ty+\Phi^T\Phi\theta+\lambda\theta.
$$
Set $\nabla J=0$:
$(\Phi^T\Phi+\lambda I)\hat\theta=\Phi^Ty$.

\Pp{BLUE $\to$ OLS}: if $R=\sigma^2I$,
$(\Phi^TR^{-1}\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^TR^{-1}y=(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^Ty$.

\Pp{Inverse-variance weights}: minimise $\sum_iw_i^2\sigma_i^2$ s.t. $\sum_iw_i=1$.
$L=\sum_iw_i^2\sigma_i^2+\lambda(\sum_iw_i-1)$,
$2w_i\sigma_i^2+\lambda=0\Rightarrow
w_i=(1/\sigma_i^2)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j^2)$.

\Pp{Gauss-Newton nonlinear LS}:
$$
H(\theta_k+\delta)\approx H(\theta_k)+J_k\delta,\quad
r_k=y-H(\theta_k),
$$
$$
\min_\delta\|r_k-J_k\delta\|_2^2,\quad
J_k^TJ_k\delta=J_k^Tr_k,\quad
\theta_{k+1}=\theta_k+\delta.
$$

\Pp{Regularisation sentence}: BLUE minimises variance only among unbiased linear estimators; ridge may be biased but can reduce MSE. Ridge shrinks; LASSO selects variables; ElasticNet combines sparsity and collinearity stability; CV selects $\lambda$.

\Pp{Stats exercise numeric OLS}: $X=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\0&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$, $y=[1,3,1]^T$, $\sigma_v^2=2$:
$\hat\theta=(X^TX)^{-1}X^Ty=[1/5,0]^T$,
$\operatorname{cov}(\hat\theta)=2(X^TX)^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}2/5&0\\0&1/3\end{bmatrix}$.

\section*{Extra Calculation Templates}

\subsection*{Quadratic ED}
If $C_i(P_i)=a_iP_i^2+b_iP_i+c_i$ and no active limits/losses:
$$
2a_iP_i+b_i=\lambda
\Rightarrow
P_i=\frac{\lambda-b_i}{2a_i},\quad
\sum_iP_i=P_D.
$$
Then $\sum_i(\lambda-b_i)/(2a_i)=P_D$ solves $\lambda$.
If computed $P_i$ violates limits, fix it at the bound and redispatch remaining demand.

\subsection*{Generic OPF Forms}
\Pp{DC OPF}:
$$
\min_{P_G,\theta}\sum_iC_i(P_{G_i})
$$
$$
\text{s.t. } P_G-P_D=B_{\rm bus}\theta,\quad
|B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j)|\le F_{ij}^{\max},
$$
$$
P_i^{\min}\le P_{G_i}\le P_i^{\max}.
$$
\Pp{AC OPF}:
$$
\min_{P_G,Q_G,V,\theta}\sum_iC_i(P_{G_i})
$$
s.t. nonlinear AC power balance, flow equations, voltage bounds, gen $P/Q$ bounds, line limits. Nonconvex due to AC equality constraints.

\Pp{SC-OPF}:
$$
\text{base-case constraints}+\text{constraints for each contingency }c\in\mathcal C.
$$

\subsection*{Exercise Copy Examples}
\Pp{Convex proof}: for $C=\{x\mid Ax\le b\}$, if $x_1,x_2\in C$,
$A(\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2)=\lambda Ax_1+(1-\lambda)Ax_2\le b$.
\Pp{Intersection}: if $x,y\in\cap_iC_i$, then $\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\in C_i$ for all $i$, hence in $\cap_iC_i$.
\Pp{Sum}: $S_1+S_2=\{u+v:u\in S_1,v\in S_2\}$; $\lambda(u_1+v_1)+(1-\lambda)(u_2+v_2)=[\lambda u_1+(1-\lambda)u_2]+[\lambda v_1+(1-\lambda)v_2]$.
\Pp{Nonnegative combination}: $f,g$ convex, $\alpha,\beta\ge0\Rightarrow \alpha f+\beta g$ convex.

\Pp{Norm cone convex}: $\Theta=\{(r,x):\|x\|\le r\}$. If $(r_i,x_i)\in\Theta$,
$\|\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2\|\le\lambda\|x_1\|+(1-\lambda)\|x_2\|\le\lambda r_1+(1-\lambda)r_2$.

\Pp{$\ell_\infty$ LP}: $\min_x\|Ax-b\|_\infty\iff
\min_{x,t}t\ \text{s.t. }-t\mathbf1\le Ax-b\le t\mathbf1$.

\Pp{$\ell_1$ LP}: $\min_x\|Ax-b\|_1\iff
\min_{x,\lambda}\mathbf1^T\lambda\ \text{s.t. }-\lambda\le Ax-b\le\lambda$.

\Pp{Exercise variants}: $\min\|Ax-b\|_1$ s.t. $\|Ax-b\|_\infty\le1$:
$\min\mathbf1^T\lambda$ s.t. $-\lambda\le Ax-b\le\lambda$, $-\mathbf1\le Ax-b\le\mathbf1$.
$\min\|x\|_1$ s.t. $\|Ax-b\|_\infty\le1$:
$\min\mathbf1^T\lambda$ s.t. $-\lambda\le x\le\lambda$, $-\mathbf1\le Ax-b\le\mathbf1$.

\Pp{$\ell_1+\ell_\infty$ LP}: $\min\|Ax-b\|_1+\|x\|_\infty\iff
\min_{\lambda,t}\mathbf1^T\lambda+t$ s.t. $-\lambda\le Ax-b\le\lambda$, $-t\mathbf1\le x\le t\mathbf1$.

\Pp{Polynomial LS}: $y_i\approx a_0+a_1x_i+\cdots+a_kx_i^k$:
$\hat\theta=(X^TX)^{-1}X^TY$, $\theta=[a_0,\ldots,a_k]^T$,
$X_{i,:}=[1,x_i,\ldots,x_i^k]$.
\Pp{Rank trap}: $X^TX$ singular if $X$ lacks full column rank, e.g. not enough/distinct $x_i$.

\Pp{Conic-section LS}: set $f=1$ in
$ax^2+bxy+cy^2+dx+ey+f=0$:
$Y=-\mathbf1$, $X_{i,:}=[x_i^2,x_iy_i,y_i^2,x_i,y_i]$,
$\hat\theta=(X^TX)^{-1}X^TY$. Classify: $b^2-4ac<0$ ellipse, $=0$ parabola, $>0$ hyperbola.

\Pp{Ellipsoid LMI}:
$$
(x-c)^TP^{-1}(x-c)\le1
\Leftrightarrow
\begin{bmatrix}
1&(x-c)^T\\
x-c&P
\end{bmatrix}\succeq0,\ P\succ0.
$$
Scalar quadratic $ax^2+2bx+c\le0$, $a>0$:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}
c+2bx & x\\
x & -1/a
\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.
$$
\Pp{Block diagonal LMI}: $F_i(x)\succeq0\ \forall i\iff
\operatorname{diag}(F_1(x),...,F_m(x))\succeq0$.

\Pp{LMI linearity}: allowed entry $3x_1-2x_2+\gamma+5$; not LMI if entries contain $x_1x_2,x^2,1/x,\sin x$, or decision-variable inverse.

\Pp{Continuous Lyapunov}: $\dot x=Ax$ stable if $\exists P\succ0$ with $A^TP+PA\prec0$. Pick $Q\succ0$, solve $A^TP+PA=-Q$.

\Pp{BLUE exercise skeleton}: $\hat\theta=Z^TY$, $Y=\Phi\theta+\epsilon$, $E\epsilon=0$, $E\epsilon\epsilon^T=R$.
\Pp{Unbiased}: $E\hat\theta=Z^T\Phi\theta=\theta\Rightarrow Z^T\Phi=I$.
\Pp{Covariance}: $\operatorname{cov}(\hat\theta)=Z^TRZ$.
\Pp{BLUE}: $\hat\theta=(\Phi^TR^{-1}\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^TR^{-1}Y$, $\operatorname{cov}=(\Phi^TR^{-1}\Phi)^{-1}$.

\Pp{Active bound KKT}: for scalar $u_{\min}\le u\le u_{\max}$, write $g_u=u-u_{\max}\le0$, $g_l=u_{\min}-u\le0$.
\Pp{If upper active}: $u=u_{\max}$, $\lambda_l=0$, check $\lambda_u\ge0$ from stationarity.
\Pp{If lower active}: $u=u_{\min}$, $\lambda_u=0$, check $\lambda_l\ge0$.

\Pp{2-bus DC OPF mini}: line $i-j$ with $P_{ij}=B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j)$.
Constraint $|P_{ij}|\le F^{\max}$ becomes $-F^{\max}\le B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j)\le F^{\max}$.
\Pp{Slack/reference}: set one angle, e.g. $\theta_1=0$.

\Pp{QP classification}: objective $\frac12x^THx+f^Tx$, $H\succeq0$, constraints $Gx\le h,\ Ax=b$.
\Pp{Unconstrained optimum}: $Hx+f=0$. If $H\succ0$, unique $x^*=-H^{-1}f$.
